mmd-002.back: About two thirds the length of the head; black edged, white inside (90%).

mmd-007.front: Is point count a good age guide?
mmd-007.back: No. The BC account says points are not reliable. Read neck, chest, belly and teeth (90%).

mmd-009.front: How do mule deer antlers branch?
mmd-009.back: Fork once about 15 to 25 cm above the base, then each branch forks again; brow tines small or absent (85%).

mmd-011.back: The Coast Range, especially in winter; hybrids where they meet (90%).

mmd-012.front: Black tail tail vs mule deer tail?
mmd-012.back: Black tail: dark brown or black on top for most of its length. Mule deer: white with a black tip only (90%).

mmd-042.front: Why does blaze orange look dull to a deer?
mmd-042.back: No red cone (75 to 85%). Motion and outline give you away.

mmd-043.back: They lack a UV filter, so UV may stand out; avoid brighteners (80%; 65% Tip).

mmd-044.back: The tapetum, a reflective layer behind the retina (80%).

mmd-046.front: What do the interdigital glands do?
mmd-046.back: Leave a scent trail as the deer walks (90%).

mmd-047.back: A lip curl that pulls urine scent to the vomeronasal organ, often by rutting bucks (65%).

mmd-048.front: Where do mule deer often bed relative to the wind?
mmd-048.back: On the leeward side of a roll, often facing downhill (65%).

mmd-049.back: Stare, head bob, foot stamp, snort, escape (70%).

mmd-050.front: A nervous mule deer walks how?

mmd-051.front: Stot: bound length and top speed?
mmd-051.back: 2.7 to 5.2 m per bound, up to about 40 km/h (80%).

mmd-052.front: Which way do mule deer flee coyotes?
mmd-052.back: Uphill; white tails go down and away (70%).

mmd-053.front: What do many mule deer do after stotting off?
mmd-053.back: Stop on a rise and look back (65%). Big old bucks often do not.

mmd-054.front: Hunted deer vs park deer flight distance?
mmd-054.back: Hunted deer flee from farther away (65%).
